newsitem.title: USA: News conference set in tobacco talks.
newsitem.headline: News conference set in tobacco talks.

text.p: A tentative 1:30 p.m. EDT news conference has been set Friday regarding a possible settlement of tobacco negotiations, according to the Mississippi Attorney General's Office.

It is expected that the terms of the deal will be announced at the conference. However, Mississippi Attorney General Mike Moore told reporters "we still got some loose ends." When asked if the deal was final he said "there's one-and-a half contentious issues left."
The states and industry officials resumed negotiations at about 9 a.m. EDT (1300 GMT) Friday and their public relations representatives were called into the meetings later.

In a sweeping agreement with U.S. states and lawyers for smokers, the tobacco companies would settle hundreds of lawsuits, launch major new anti-smoking programmes, sharply curtail cigarette advertising and submit to tough new government regulation.

Sources close to the talks said the industry had made major concessions in the area of Food and Drug Administration regulation that would give the government agency the power to regulate cigarettes as a drug delivery device.

The sources said the parties plan to propose a total settlement package of about $370 billion. Part of the package, about $50 billion, would be to "punish" the industry. That amount would be used to pay for health coverage for uninsured children, sources said.
